title: The value of random zero-sum games
summary: We study the value of a two-player zero-sum game on a random matrix $M\in \mathbb{R}^{n\times m}$, defined by $v(M) = \min_{x\inΔ_n}\max_{y\in Δ_m}x^T M y$. In the setting where $n=m$ and $M$ has i.i.d. standard Gaussian entries, we prove that the standard deviation of $v(M)$ is of order $\frac{1}{n}$. This confirms an experimental conjecture dating back to the 1980s. We also investigate the case where $M$ is a rectangular Gaussian matrix with $m = n+λ\sqrt{n}$, showing that the expected value of the game is of order $\fracλ{n}$, as well as the case where $M$ is a random orthogonal matrix.…
